newsitem.title: CHINA: Caterpillar in $98 mln China castings venture.
newsitem.headline: Caterpillar in $98 mln China castings venture.

text.p: A joint venture linking Caterpillar Inc of the U.S. and investment firm ASIMCO with a major Chinese conglomerate calls for investment of $98 million, the official Xinhua news agency said on Tuesday.
The venture with the China International Trust and Investment Corp was announced last week but no value for the deal had been given.
The plant in Shanxi province will produce castings for medium and heavy-duty diesel engines, ASIMCO (Asian Strategic Investments Corp) said last week.
ASIMCO will own 57 percent of the company, Caterpillar 21 percent, and CITIC subsidiary CITIC Machinery and Manufacturing Co (CMMI) the remaining 22 percent, Xinhua said.

The company is scheduled to begin operation in the first quarter of 1998, and is expected to produce 45,000 tonnes of castings in the first phase, and another 40,000 tonnes after the second phase goes into operation.
ASIMCO is a Beijing-based but U.S.-managed direct investment that already has 17 joint ventures in China, 13 of them in auto parts and components.
CMMI is a large military-turned-civilian enterprise with fixed assets totalling 1.6 billion yuan.
Caterpillar was to provide casting technology while ASIMCO and China International Trust would supply capital, facilities, machinery and personnel.
The venture would use CMMI's existing foundry in Shanxi, an area with large supplies of coal and pig iron needed for the project.
China International Trust has interests in manufacturing, telecommunications and finance and has a substantial stake in Hong Kong-listed CITIC Pacific Ltd.
